title: acme-logistics: making Billing separately releasable
subtitle: How to get Billing into its own release without stopping the system, in steps that each leave it working and can be undone.

verdict.text: Do it, because Billing is cheaper to separate than most modules: only its own code touches its tables and no transaction crosses the boundary. Go through step 11 and keep Billing on the same Postgres, but if only the stopping hurts and not the shared release, step 2 alone fixes that.

stats.label: Tables with two writers
stats.note: shipments, not Billing's; invoices gets a temporary one in steps 5 to 10

stats.label: Main pain ends
stats.note: Billing issues invoices from the queue

sections.title: The gap
sections.intro: Billing is small and already mostly separate in its data. What ties it down is one call inside a request, one response body and a release that has no way to avoid a restart.

rows: Billing ships inside the `api` image. Of 16 commits, 14 changed `src/` and 3 changed Billing code.
Only 3 of 14 API image changes concerned Billing, yet any release restarts both.
One `api` instance, no proxy and no health check in the repo [high]
Two instances behind a proxy, Billing released on its own
A restart today takes shipments, tracking and invoices down together.
Billing imports 4 modules. Billing and Shipments import each other (`BillingService.cs:4`, `ShipmentService.cs:2`).
No reference to `Acme.Logistics` in either direction
Billing cannot be built alone while the cycle exists.
A direct call inside the `/delivered` request (`ShipmentService.cs:118`)
Billing consumes `shipment.delivered`, already published at `ShipmentService.cs:117` with 0 consumers
Billing can then stop while deliveries continue.
Returns the invoice `number` and `total` (`ShipmentsController.cs:52`). 0 callers in this repo [high].
This one contract is what stands in the way of the queue.
`invoices` and `invoice_numbers`: 4 SQL statements, all in `BillingService.cs`, no join to other tables [high]
Stay as they are, in the same Postgres
The usually hard part is already done.
0 in the repo. Each statement opens its own connection (`Database.cs:17`) [high].
No transaction has to be unpicked.
Published with no properties and no confirm (`MessageBus.cs:25`), so not persistent [med]
A lost event costs nothing today. After the cut it costs an invoice.
A second `/delivered` issues a second invoice; only cancelled shipments are refused (`ShipmentService.cs:110`) [high]
A queue can deliver a message twice.
Contract tests and a schema baseline
There is nothing to prove each step against.

blocks.title: A smaller target
blocks.text: If what hurts is the system stopping, and not Billing sharing a release with the rest, **step 2 alone** fixes it for every module. Steps 3 and 4 add a real boundary and pay for themselves. The full plan is worth it only if Billing needs its own release schedule, and its history is quiet so far: 3 commits, all by one author.

items: `GET /api/invoices?shipmentId=` and `POST /api/invoices/{number}/credit` keep their URL, status code and JSON fields.
`POST /api/shipments/{id}/delivered` keeps its body until every caller has stopped reading the invoice from it (step 9).
A delivery recorded through `/delivered` produces an invoice, and a Billing release never loses one.
From step 6, a shipment has at most one live invoice. Until then duplicates behave as they do today.
Invoice numbers keep the format `ACME-yyyy-NNNNNN` and keep coming from `invoice_numbers`.
VAT at 20% and its rounding do not change. The shadow run in step 8 proves it on real deliveries.
Existing invoices are not rewritten or moved.
Old and new versions run side by side in every release, so each schema or message change must work for both.
From step 10, booking, tracking and confirming delivery keep working while Billing is down.
Deliveries the worker detects are not invoiced today. This plan keeps that until someone decides otherwise (see Open questions).

sections.title: The steps
sections.intro: Ordered by what unblocks the rest. File references are to today's code. Sizes compare steps with each other and say nothing about time.

nodes.label: Move callers, issue from the queue

items.title: 1. Pin today's behaviour
items.text:
**Changes:** the repo's first tests: contracts for `GET /api/invoices`, `POST /api/invoices/{number}/credit` and `POST /api/shipments/{id}/delivered`, plus VAT, number format and what a second `/delivered` does. Dump the live schema into the repo (`pg_dump -s`), since no table is defined anywhere in it. Log who calls `/delivered` and `/credit`.

**Stays:** all production behaviour.

items.title: 2. Put a proxy in front and run two API instances
items.text:
**Changes:** a new `edge` service takes all `/api/*` traffic and still sends it to `api`. The API gets `/healthz` and runs as two instances, restarted one at a time. The worker calls the edge instead of `api:8080`. The API holds no state in memory, so two instances are safe [high].

**Stays:** every URL and response.

**Pays by itself:** API releases stop interrupting the system, which also covers every later step.

items.title: 3. Break the Billing and Shipments cycle
items.text:
**Changes:** `IssueInvoiceAsync` takes a shipment id and a net amount instead of a `Shipment` (`BillingService.cs:17,25-31`). The delivered check at `BillingService.cs:19-22` moves to the caller, which has just set that status (`ShipmentService.cs:115`). `ShipmentService` calls a port it owns, returning a small receipt (`ShipmentService.cs:30,107,118`), and an adapter in `Acme.Api` connects it to Billing (`Program.cs:14`).

**Stays:** the order of status update, publish and invoice, and the `/delivered` body.

items.title: 4. Give Billing its own project
items.text:
**Changes:** a new `src/Acme.Billing` with no reference to `Acme.Logistics`. Move `BillingService.cs`, `Invoice.cs` and `AddVat`, whose only caller is Billing. Copy `Money` (26 lines) and `Database` (33 lines), neither changed since the first commit, plus `CleanText` and `FormatDate`. Add a test that fails on any reference across the boundary.

**Stays:** one deployable, one process. Billing no longer uses `Domain`, so the Domain and Infrastructure cycle stops mattering to this work.

items.title: 5. Billing service takes /api/invoices
items.text:
**Changes:** a thin `Acme.Billing.Host` with a copy of `InvoicesController` (same routes, same JSON), `/healthz`, its own image and compose service. The edge sends `/api/invoices*` to it.

**Stays:** issuing, still in the API, and the old controller, kept for routing back.

**Temporary:** `invoices` has two writers until step 10: the API inserts and Billing sets `credited`.

**Pays by itself:** a real independent release, on low-risk traffic.

items.title: 6. One live invoice per shipment
items.text:
**Changes:** check live data for duplicates, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on `invoices (shipment_id) WHERE NOT credited`. Issuing looks for a live invoice first, inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and returns the existing one.

**Stays:** a credited invoice can be issued again.

**Behaviour change:** a second `/delivered` no longer creates a second invoice. The queue needs this, and it fixes a defect by itself. Needs a yes (ADR 3).

items.title: 7. Make the delivered event safe to depend on
items.text:
**Changes:** add `netAmount`, `currency` and `deliveredAt` to `shipment.delivered`, keeping `id`. Publish persistently and wait for the broker's confirm. Add a contract test on a JSON fixture rather than a shared library.

**Stays:** adding fields is safe, because the only binding anywhere is `shipment.booked` (`tracking.py:35`) [high].

items.title: 8. Shadow run
items.text:
**Changes:** Billing binds a durable queue to `shipment.delivered`. For each event it computes net and VAT and compares them with the row the API wrote. It issues nothing and takes no number.

**Stays:** the API's invoice is still the real one.

items.title: 9. Move callers off the invoice in the /delivered response
items.text:
**Changes:** using the log from step 1, move each caller to `GET /api/invoices?shipmentId=`, which already returns number and total.

**Stays:** the response body, until step 10.

**If a caller cannot move:** keep the body and have the API wait briefly for the invoice, returning nulls if Billing is away.

items.title: 10. Billing issues from the queue
items.text:
**Changes:** switch Billing from shadow to issuing, acknowledging only after the commit, with a dead-letter queue. Then flip the API's flag so the port does nothing. During the flip both may try, and the index from step 6 lets only one through. `/delivered` returns `number` and `total` as null.

**Stays:** the event, the tables and every URL.

**The main pain ends here:** a Billing release touches nothing else, and deliveries wait in the queue.

items.title: 11. Remove the old path
items.text:
**Changes:** after a full billing period on the new path, delete the in-process adapter and flag, the API's `InvoicesController`, the API's reference to Billing, the old Billing code, `AddVat`, and `number` and `total` from the `/delivered` body.

**Stays:** everything Billing does.

items.title: 12. Optional: a database role only Billing holds
items.text:
**Changes:** a `billing` role with rights only on `invoices` and `invoice_numbers`, with those rights revoked from the shared `acme` role.

**Stays:** the tables, where they are. This turns a convention into a rule the database enforces.

blocks.text:
**The main pain ends at step 10**, when a Billing release no longer touches anything else. Do step 11 straight after the bake period, because two live issuing paths are the worst place to stay. Step 12 is optional.

Steps 1 to 4 each pay on their own, so stopping after any of them leaves a better system with nothing half done. Steps 5 to 11 are one unit: once `invoices` has a second writer, finish.

items: **The Domain and Infrastructure cycle** (`Parcel.cs:1`, `ShipmentRepository.cs:2`). Billing stops using `Domain` at step 4, so it no longer stands in the way.
**The two writers on `shipments`** (`ShipmentRepository.cs:68`, `db.py:11`) and **the API and worker call loop**. Neither involves Billing unless open question 2 is answered yes.
**A separate database.** Only Billing touches its tables, so a second instance adds backups and cost and buys nothing yet.
**A separate repository.** An own image and release are enough.
**A shared library for `Money` or the event.** It would bring back releasing in lock-step. A 26-line copy and a contract test are cheaper.
**A transactional outbox.** Today a crash between the status update and the invoice insert also loses the invoice, so this plan is no worse. Add one if a lost invoice ever appears.
**Pricing written twice** (`PricingRules.cs`, `pricing.ts`, changed together in 6 of 6 commits). It costs more day to day than Billing does and deserves its own plan.

sections.title: ADR drafts
sections.intro: Drafts only. None goes into the repo without a yes.

blocks.title: ADR 1: Billing is a separate deployable on the shared Postgres
blocks.code:
Status: proposed

Context: Billing ships inside the API image, so any release of either restarts both.
Only Billing code touches invoices and invoice_numbers.

Decision: Billing gets its own project, image and release, in this repository.
It keeps its tables in the same Postgres instance. It shares no code with Acme.Logistics;
Money and Database are copied, and contracts are checked by tests on JSON fixtures.

Consequences: Billing releases alone. Small copies may drift, by design.
A separate database stays possible and is not planned.

blocks.title: ADR 2: Invoices are issued from the shipment.delivered event
blocks.code:
Status: proposed

Context: Issuing inside the /delivered request means Shipments needs Billing to be up.

Decision: Shipments publishes shipment.delivered, persistent and confirmed, with the net
amount and currency. Billing consumes it and acknowledges after the commit.
POST /api/shipments/{id}/delivered no longer returns the invoice; callers read
GET /api/invoices?shipmentId=.

Consequences: Billing can stop while deliveries continue. An invoice appears shortly
after delivery instead of in the response. A crash between the status update and the
publish loses the invoice, as a crash before the insert does today.

blocks.title: ADR 3: One live invoice per shipment
blocks.code:
Status: proposed

Context: A second /delivered creates a second invoice, and a queue can deliver twice.

Decision: Unique index on invoices (shipment_id) WHERE NOT credited. Issuing returns
the existing live invoice instead of creating another.

Consequences: This changes behaviour. Duplicates already in the data must be resolved
first. A credited invoice can still be issued again.

items: **Who calls `POST /api/shipments/{id}/delivered`?** Nothing in this repo does. It blocks step 9, and the fallback there applies if a caller cannot move.

**Should deliveries the worker detects be invoiced?** The worker writes Delivered directly (`tracking.py:24`) and the API ignores that report (`ShipmentService.cs:133`), so those shipments get no invoice and no event. That this happens is checked [high]. Whether it is intended is not known, and if it is not, it is a billing defect today.

**Do the row mappings work?** `InvoiceRow` and `ShipmentRow` need column mapping that is not in the repo (no `MatchNamesWithUnderscores`, no type handler for `Money` or `Parcel`), so I expect those reads to fail as written [med]. Nothing was run. Step 1 will settle it, and if they fail, fix that before pinning.

**What is the real schema?** Step 6 needs to know whether live duplicates exist and whether `credited` can be null. A foreign key from `invoices` to `shipments` would matter only for a separate database.
**Can accounting accept gaps in invoice numbers?** Postgres sequences can already leave gaps, and the flip in step 10 could add a few [med].

blocks.title: What I assumed
items: "Release on its own" means an own image and release, in this repository.
"Without stopping the system" covers both this migration and every later Billing release.
Production runs like `docker-compose.yml` on one host, or equivalent. If a proxy already sits in front, use it in step 2 instead of adding `edge`.
An invoice may appear shortly after delivery rather than in the response.
`edge` is nginx because it is one config file. Any proxy will do.
